author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1953-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: The purpose of practicing detachment is to separate us from our present reactions to life and attach us to our aim in life.
context_before: want to make visible, we now set about the task of entering such a state, for we must move psychologically from where we are to where we desire to be.
context_after: This inner separation must be developed by practice. At first we seem to have no power to separate ourselves from undesirable inner states, simply because we have always taken every mood, every reaction, as natural and have become identified with them. When we have no idea that our reactions are only states of consciousness from which it is possible to separate ourselves, we go round and round in the same circle of problems – not seeing them as inner states but as outer situations. We practice detachment, or inner separation, that we may escape from the circle of our habitual reactions to life. That is why we must formulate an aim and constantly notice ourselves in regard to that aim.
